newsitem.title: USA: BMW to add head airbags for side impacts.
newsitem.headline: BMW to add head airbags for side impacts.

text.p: BMW of North America Inc said on Wednesday it will begin equipping its 7 Series cars with new airbags for head protection in side impacts, making BMW the first automaker in the world to offer such devices.

The new head protection system will begin showing up this June as a standard feature and will eventually be available on all BMW sedans, said Henrich Heitmann, chairman and chief executive officer of BMW (US) Holding Corp, a unit of Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG.
Heitmann spoke at a breakfast meeting that kicked off the press days for the New York International Auto Show.

The new head airbag is a long tube that is stored in the roof panel above each front door. Upon impact, it inflates and protects a passenger's head and neck from the windshield pillar, window and center pillar.
The new head protection system, which will be on both sides of the car, is not expected to add significantly to the cost of the car, Heitmann said.
According to BMW, about 21 percent of all motor vehicle accidents are side impact collisions, accounting for 36 percent of all fatalities.
BMW currently offers side impact airbags in its 3 Series sedans, all 5 Series models and 7 Series models.

In his remarks, Heitmann said BMW will this year enter the heavyweight cruiser segment of the motorcyle industry with a new bike called the BMW Cruiser. Annual worldwide sales volume for the Cruiser will be about 10,000 units. Only about 1,500 are expected to be available in the U.S. in 1997.
